title: Acetaminophen produces limited molecular and functional effects in human cortical organoids
title_zh: 对人类皮质类器官的乙酰氨基酚产生有限的分子与功能影响
abstract: Abstract Acetaminophen (APAP) is the most widely used analgesic during pregnancy, yet its effects on prenatal human brain development remain incompletely understood. Epidemiological studies have reported inconsistent associations between prenatal APAP exposure and later neurodevelopmental outcomes, underscoring the need for mechanistic evaluation in human-relevant developmental models. Here, we examined how APAP influences early cortical development using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cortical organoids (COs) generated from six independent lines. Organoids were exposed to physiologically relevant APAP concentrations (25, 50, and 100 μM) for 5 days beginning at day 21 of differentiation, corresponding to late first-trimester cortical development. We assessed organoid growth, apoptosis, differentiation, synaptic maturation, transcriptomic profiles using bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), and functional network activity using multielectrode array recordings up to 4 months. APAP exposure did not affect organoid size, cytoarchitecture, or viability. Neuronal and progenitor cell proportions, as well as synaptic puncta density were unchanged. Bulk RNA-seq revealed subtle transcriptional changes only at the highest dose (16 differentially expressed genes at 100 μM), enriched for neurodevelopmental pathways. In contrast, snRNA-seq at 3 months revealed no changes in cell type composition or gene expression. Consistent with the limited molecular changes observed, electrophysiological measures including firing rate, burst frequency, and network synchrony, showed no significant differences from controls. Together, these results indicate that direct exposure to parent APAP at the concentrations tested produces minimal molecular perturbations. These findings reflect responses to parent acetaminophen in vitro and do not exclude metabolite-mediated or systemic effects in vivo.
abstract_zh: 摘要 乙酰氨基酚（APAP）是孕期最常用的镇痛药，但其对胎儿大脑发育的影响尚未完全阐明。流行病学研究报告了孕期APAP暴露与后期神经发育结果之间不一致的关联，凸显了在与人类相关的发育模型中进行机制评估的必要性。我们利用来自六条独立细胞系的诱导多能干细胞（iPSC）衍生皮质类器官（COs）研究APAP对早期皮质发育的影响。类器官在分化第21天开始暴露于生理相关的APAP浓度（25、50和100 μM）5天，对应于第一孕晚期的皮质发育。我们评估了类器官的生长、凋亡、分化、突触成熟、使用批量和单核RNA测序（snRNA-seq）的转录组特征，以及多电极阵列记录至4个月的功能网络活动。APAP暴露未影响类器官大小、细胞结构或存活率。神经元和祖细胞比例以及突触点密度保持不变。批量RNA-seq仅在最高剂量（100 μM）下显示细微的转录变化（16个差异表达基因），富集于神经发育通路。相反，3个月时的snRNA-seq未发现细胞类型组成或基因表达的变化。与有限的分子变化一致，电生理测量（如放电率、爆发频率和网络同步性）与对照组无显著差异。综上所述，直接暴露于所测浓度的原始APAP产生的分子扰动最小。这些发现反映了体外对原始乙酰氨基酚的响应，并不排除体内代谢物介导或系统性效应。
